summary:
### TL;DR
- **`pull_request_target` will be blocked by default in all public repositories starting December 2, 2026.** The original date was November 2, 2026. Brownouts are scheduled for **November 9 and November 16 (16:00–18:00 UTC)**. Review the Insights view and update your Actions event policies before November 9. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-02-pull_request_target-blocked-by-default-december-2))
- Code security and secret risk assessments now show whether findings are in **protected or unprotected repositories**. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-02-security-risk-assessments-include-repository-protection-status))
- Private vulnerability reports now have documented **rate limits**. Maintainers can change their repository's limit and exempt trusted reporters. ([source](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/424fb583412143b8e8fc8160b82e540ffa1d6cdc))

### Action required
- **`pull_request_target` blocked by default on December 2, 2026** ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-02-pull_request_target-blocked-by-default-december-2))
  - **Scope:** Public repositories on GitHub Free, Team, and Enterprise Cloud. Private and internal repositories and GitHub Enterprise Server are not affected.
  - **What gets blocked:** `pull_request_target` events are blocked unless an applicable Actions event policy explicitly allows them.
  - **Current state:** The rule comes from workflow execution protections and is running in evaluate mode. Affected workflows still run but show warnings.
  - **Brownouts:**

    | Date | Time (UTC) |
    |---|---|
    | November 9, 2026 | 16:00–18:00 |
    | November 16, 2026 | 16:00–18:00 |

    During these windows, blocked workflows will not execute. Instead, they create failed runs with an error annotation.
  - **What to do before November 9:**
    1. Use Insights to find which runs the rule would block.
    2. Decide, per workflow, whether to keep the block or allow the trigger.
    3. If a workflow genuinely needs `pull_request_target`, allow it in an Actions event policy. Use workflow file targeting to allow only specific workflows.
    4. While doing this, audit those workflows for execution of untrusted fork code, since `pull_request_target` has access to base-repository secrets.

### Security improvements
- **Risk assessments show protection status.** ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-02-security-risk-assessments-include-repository-protection-status))
  - Findings are now marked as being in protected or unprotected repositories, which shows where to extend coverage.
  - Organization admins and security managers start assessments from Security tab → Assessments.
  - Available in GitHub Enterprise Cloud and GitHub Team.
  - The secret risk assessment version comes to GitHub Enterprise Server 3.24.
- **Rate limits for private vulnerability reports** (documented). ([commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/424fb583412143b8e8fc8160b82e540ffa1d6cdc))
  - Each reporter can submit at most 25 reports per 24 hours across repositories where they are not a trusted reporter.
  - Each reporter can submit at most 5 reports to a single repository per 24 hours.
  - By default, a repository accepts at most 10 reports per 24 hours from all reporters combined.
  - Maintainers can raise or lower their repository's total limit and exempt trusted reporters. Reports from trusted reporters do not count toward that repository's limits or toward the reporter's global limit.
- **Dependabot supports the APM package manager.** ([commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/e755a938bb80e20228732a352ba8c54b4ff90bfd))
  - The YAML value is `apm`.
  - APM supports both default-days and SemVer-bump-days `cooldown` settings.
  - The docs gate this content behind a version flag, so availability may vary by product.

### Docs changes worth reading
- **[Configure private vulnerability reporting for a repository](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/report-and-fix-vulnerabilities/configure-vulnerability-reporting/configure-for-a-repository):** New section explaining the rate limits and the steps to set a custom repository limit or exempt trusted reporters.
- **[Report a vulnerability privately](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/report-and-fix-vulnerabilities/report-privately):** New section listing the per-reporter and per-repository limits. It also explains that each 24-hour period starts with the first report that counts toward the limit, and that reporters see a message when they hit a limit.
- **[Dependabot options reference](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference):** APM added to the `cooldown` support table and the package-ecosystem table (`apm`, supported versions "Not applicable").
- **[Interpret code security risk assessment](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/tutorials/secure-your-organization/interpret-code-security-risk-assessment):**
  - Metrics now break down vulnerabilities by protected repositories (GitHub Code Security enabled) versus unprotected ones.
  - The "Repositories scanned" table now includes each repository's protection status.
- **[Interpret secret risk assessment](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/tutorials/secure-your-organization/interpret-secret-risk-assessment):** Metrics now break down secrets by protected repositories (GitHub Secret Protection enabled) versus unprotected ones.

changelog.title: Security risk assessments include repository protection status
changelog.text: The GitHub code security risk assessment and secret risk assessment now show whether findings are in protected or unprotected repositories, helping you identify where to extend your security coverage. Organization admins and security managers can start an assessment by going to Assessments under their organization’s Security tab. This improvement is available in GitHub Enterprise Cloud and GitHub Team. It will be available for the secret risk assessment in GitHub Enterprise Server 3.24. Read more in the code security risk assessment documentation and secret risk assessment documentation . The post Security risk assessments include repository protection status appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: pull_request_target blocked by default December 2
changelog.text: Starting December 2, 2026, GitHub Actions will block pull_request_target events by default in all public repositories, unless an applicable Actions event policy explicitly allows them. Enforcement was previously scheduled for November 2, 2026. GitHub introduced this default rule through workflow execution protections. The rule initially runs in evaluate mode, so you can see which workflow runs it would block before enforcement begins. Private and internal repositories aren’t affected. Why we’re making this change pull_request_target runs in the context of the base repository and can access its secrets. If a workflow executes untrusted code from a fork, that code could compromise your pipeline or steal secrets. The default rule helps reduce this risk while letting you explicitly allow workflows that depend on the trigger. Brownout schedule Before permanent enforcement begins on December 2, 2026, we’ll temporarily enforce the default protection during two scheduled brownouts. These windows will help you identify affected workflows and update your policies before enforcement becomes permanent. Date Time (UTC) November 9, 2026 16:00–18:00 November 16, 2026 16:00–18:00 During each window, pull_request_target workflow attempts blocked by the default rule in affected public repositories will create failed runs with an error annotation; the workflows won’t execute. After each window, the default rule will return to evaluate mode, allowing workflows to run with warnings. Private and internal repositories aren’t affected. Prepare your workflows Before the first brownout on November 9, use Insights to see which workflow runs the rule would block. From there, you have two options: Keep the default rule in place to block pull_request_target . Explicitly allow pull_request_target in an applicable Actions event policy if your workflows depend on it. Use workflow file targeting to allow specific workflows. See how to control workflow execution to configure your policies. This change applies to public repositories on GitHub Free, GitHub Team, and GitHub Enterprise Cloud, not GitHub Enterprise Server. The post pull_request_target blocked by default December 2 appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
